x: Statement I is correct: Recent scientific studies, including those from ETH Zurich published in Nature Geoscience and PNAS, have confirmed that the Earth's rotation and its axis are shifting. Statement III is correct and explains Statement I: The ETH Zurich study clearly states that climate change is melting polar ice, and the resulting water redistributes toward the equator. s: The Earth completes one rotation on its axis in

s: The movement of the Earth on its axis is called as ……… .
x: Earth's spinning on its own axis is called rotation. Revolution is its movement around the Sun.

s: If the earth rotates faster than its present speed, the acceleration due to gravity will
o: Increase at the equator but remain unchanged at the poles.
decrease at the equator but remain unchanged at the poles.
remain unchanged at the equator but decrease at the poles.
remain unchanged at the equator but increase at the poles.
x: Centrifugal force from rotation is maximum at the Equator and zero at the poles. Faster rotation would increase it at the Equator, which reduces effective gravity there, while gravity at the poles stays unchanged.

s: What causes the wind to deflect toward the left in the southern hemisphere?
x: Deflection of winds to the right in the northern hemisphere and to the left in the southern hemisphere is due to the Coriolis force. Coriolis force arises due to the rotation of the earth on its axis.

s:
Consider the given statements.

I. Coriolis effect is zero at the Equator.

II. Coriolis effect is more towards the Poles.

III. Coriolis effects are related to the decreasing rotational velocity with increasing latitudes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Coriolis force is 2Ωv sin(latitude), so it is zero at the Equator and maximum at the poles. It grows with latitude, which is why all three statements are accepted.

s: The Coriolis effect is the result of
x: Coriolis effect is the apparent deflection of moving air and water caused by Earth's rotation, not by revolution or tilt.

s: The weight of human body is
o: same at every place on the earth’s surface.
more on the mountains than planes.
x: Centrifugal force from rotation is greatest at the Equator and zero at the poles, so weight is least at the Equator and greatest at the poles. Weight is therefore not the same everywhere.

s: Wind in the northern hemisphere is deflected towards right due to —
x: The deflection of winds in the Northern Hemisphere toward the right is caused by the Coriolis effect, which results from the rotation of the Earth. This effect influences global wind patterns, ocean currents and weather systems.

s: What causes wind to deflect towards the left in the Southern Hemisphere?
x: The deflection of winds is caused by the Coriolis force, which arises due to the rotation of the Earth. In the Southern Hemisphere, this force deflects moving air to the left, while in the Northern Hemisphere, it deflects winds to the right. Temperature, pressure and magnetic field do not directly cause the directional deflection of winds.

s: In completing one revolution of the sun, Earth takes approximately –
x: The Earth takes 365.25636 days or 365 days, 6 hours, 9 minutes and 9.51 second to complete one orbit around the Sun. This period is known as ‘Solar year’. The solar year is also known as The tropical year. The tropical year is equal to 365.24 days. In the year 2000, an increase of 5 minute had been noted in comparison to other years. In this period the time was calculated to 365 days, 6 hours, 13 minutes (in place of 9 minutes), 53.26 seconds (in place of 9.51 seconds). Such a year is known as the ‘Anomalistic Year’.
